note: Stored refresher questions, one short multiple-choice question per concept (contracts/v2/concepts.json). Answers and explanations are private: the public shape matches the plan question (contracts/v2 §1). Lane A2 grades via app.profile.skills.lookup_refresher(questionId).

questions.title: Reassignment
questions.prompt: Python: `a = 3`, then `b = a`, then `a = 5`. What is `b`?
questions.explanation: `b = a` copies the value 3 at that moment; rebinding `a` later does not change `b`.

questions.title: String and int
questions.prompt: Python: what does `int("7") + 3` evaluate to?
questions.explanation: `int("7")` converts the string to the integer 7, so the sum is 10.

questions.title: Integer division
questions.prompt: Python: what is `17 // 5` and `17 % 5`?
questions.explanation: `//` is floor division (17 // 5 = 3) and `%` is the remainder (17 - 15 = 2).

questions.title: Slicing
questions.prompt: Python: what is `"breakpoint"[0:5]`?
questions.explanation: A slice includes the start index and stops before the end index: characters 0 to 4.

questions.title: What input returns
questions.prompt: Python: the user types 42 at `x = input()`. What is `type(x)`?
questions.explanation: `input()` always returns a string; convert it with `int(x)` when you need a number.

questions.title: First true branch
questions.prompt: With `x = 15`: `if x > 10: print("A")` / `elif x > 5: print("B")` / `else: print("C")`. What prints?
questions.explanation: Only the first branch whose condition is true runs; `elif` is skipped once `if` matched.

questions.title: Counting iterations
questions.prompt: How many times does the body of `for i in range(2, 10, 3):` run?
questions.explanation: range(2, 10, 3) yields 2, 5 and 8; the stop value 10 is excluded.

questions.title: Return vs print
questions.prompt: Python: `def f(x): print(x * 2)`. What is the value of `y` after `y = f(3)`?
questions.explanation: The function prints 6 but has no `return`, so it returns None.

questions.title: Base case
questions.prompt: What happens if a recursive function has no reachable base case?

choices.text: It recurses until the call stack overflows

questions.explanation: Every call makes another call, so the stack grows until the runtime raises a recursion/stack-overflow error.

questions.title: finally
questions.prompt: In `try: ... except ValueError: ... finally: ...`, when does the `finally` block run?
questions.explanation: `finally` runs whether the try block succeeded, raised a handled error, or raised an unhandled one.

questions.title: Negative index
questions.prompt: Python: with `nums = [4, 8, 15, 16]`, what is `nums[-1] + nums[1]`?
questions.explanation: `nums[-1]` is the last item (16) and `nums[1]` is the second item (8): 16 + 8 = 24.

questions.title: Missing key
questions.prompt: Python: `d = {"a": 1}`. What does `d.get("b", 0)` return?
questions.explanation: `get` returns the default (0) when the key is missing instead of raising KeyError.

questions.title: Duplicates
questions.prompt: Python: what is `len(set([1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3]))`?
questions.explanation: A set keeps one copy of each value: {1, 2, 3}.

questions.title: LIFO vs FIFO
questions.prompt: Push 1, 2, 3 onto a stack, then pop once. Which value comes out?
questions.explanation: A stack is last-in, first-out, so the most recent push (3) is popped first. A queue would return 1.

questions.title: Access cost
questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of reading the k-th element of a singly linked list?
questions.explanation: You must follow k `next` pointers from the head; there is no direct indexing.

questions.title: BST in-order
questions.prompt: An in-order traversal of a binary search tree visits the keys in which order?
questions.explanation: Left subtree, node, right subtree: in a BST that is exactly ascending key order.

questions.title: Shortest path, unweighted
questions.prompt: Which traversal finds the fewest-edges path in an unweighted graph?
questions.explanation: BFS explores nodes in order of distance (number of edges) from the start.

questions.title: Min-heap peek
questions.prompt: In a min-heap, where is the smallest element?
questions.explanation: The heap property keeps every parent <= its children, so the minimum is the root (O(1) to read).

questions.title: Merge sort cost
questions.prompt: What is merge sort's worst-case time complexity?
questions.explanation: It halves the input log n times and merges n items at each level, in every case.

questions.title: Binary search precondition
questions.prompt: What must be true of an array before you binary-search it?

choices.text: Its length is a power of two

questions.explanation: Binary search discards half the range by comparing with the middle, which only works on sorted data.

questions.title: Pair sum
questions.prompt: To find two numbers summing to a target in a sorted array with two pointers, what do you do when the current sum is too small?
questions.explanation: Moving the left pointer right picks a larger value, which is the only way to increase the sum.

questions.title: Why memoize
questions.prompt: Why does memoizing naive recursive Fibonacci make it much faster?

choices.text: Each subproblem is computed once instead of exponentially many times

questions.explanation: Overlapping subproblems are cached, turning O(2^n) calls into O(n).

questions.title: When greedy fails
questions.prompt: With coins {1, 3, 4}, a greedy 'largest coin first' strategy for amount 6 uses how many coins?
questions.explanation: Greedy picks 4 + 1 + 1 = 3 coins, but 3 + 3 = 2 coins is optimal: greedy is not always correct.

questions.title: Nested loops
questions.prompt: Two nested loops, each running over all n items, do constant work inside. What is the time complexity?
questions.explanation: The inner body runs n times for each of n outer iterations: n x n.

questions.title: self
questions.prompt: Python: in `def area(self):` inside a class, what is `self`?

choices.text: The instance the method was called on

questions.explanation: `obj.area()` passes `obj` as the first argument, conventionally named `self`.

questions.title: map
questions.prompt: Python: what is `list(map(lambda x: x * x, [1, 2, 3]))`?
questions.explanation: `map` applies the function to each item: 1, 4, 9.

questions.title: WHERE vs HAVING
questions.prompt: Which clause filters rows before grouping?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before GROUP BY; HAVING filters groups afterwards.

questions.title: LEFT JOIN
questions.prompt: `customers LEFT JOIN orders ON ...`: what happens to a customer with no orders?

choices.text: The customer appears once with NULL order columns
The customer is matched to every order

questions.explanation: A LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table and fills unmatched right-side columns with NULL.

questions.title: Event listener
questions.prompt: Which call runs `onClick` every time a button is clicked?
questions.explanation: Pass the function itself; `onClick()` would call it once immediately and register its return value.

questions.title: Event loop order
questions.prompt: What does this log? `console.log(1); setTimeout(() => console.log(2), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log(3)); console.log(4);`
questions.explanation: Synchronous code first (1, 4), then microtasks (promise: 3), then timers (2).

questions.title: Props
questions.prompt: Can a React child component modify the props it receives?

choices.text: No, props are read-only; the parent passes a callback to change its state

questions.explanation: Data flows down; a child asks the parent to change by calling a function passed as a prop.

questions.title: Stale state
questions.prompt: With `const [n, setN] = useState(0)`, a click handler calls `setN(n + 1); setN(n + 1);`. What is n after one click?
questions.explanation: Both calls read the same `n` (0) from this render. Use `setN(prev => prev + 1)` to get 2.

questions.title: Status codes
questions.prompt: An API returns 404. What does that mean?

choices.text: The requested resource was not found

questions.explanation: 4xx codes are client errors; 404 Not Found means no resource at that URL. 500 is a server error, 401 unauthenticated, 204 no content.

questions.title: Staging
questions.prompt: What does `git add file.py` do?

choices.text: Pushes the file to the remote
Stages the file's current changes for the next commit

questions.explanation: `git add` moves changes into the staging area; `git commit` records them; `git push` uploads commits.

questions.title: Unit test
questions.prompt: What makes a good unit test?

choices.text: It checks one behaviour in isolation with a clear expected result
It calls the real production database
It prints output for a human to read

questions.explanation: Unit tests are small, fast and deterministic: one behaviour, isolated dependencies, an assertion.
